title: Run JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule
summary: In src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp I moved the JoinDependentFilterRule registration to just before DistributivityRule. Nothing else changed. Before, DistributivityRule pulled the shared join-key equality out of the root OR first, so JoinDependentFilterRule never saw an OR and derived no per-table filters. With the new order it derives the per-table OR filters, and they get pushed down to the scans. The build is OK and bench results match. Bench, best vs mine: q19 378→204ms (-45.9%), then 353→185ms (-47.6%) on a rerun. Visible geomean -4.6%. No other template moved beyond noise. q04 showed +5.5% and +5.1% on two runs, then -3.6% on a third. q04 has no OR predicate, so the rule cannot touch its plan, which means this is noise. I did not run the optimizer unit tests (test/optimizer/*) or plan-snapshot tests, because only dbe-tool can be run here.
notes: This repeats an earlier run's result (q19 -53% then, -46..-48% now). A follow-up could check whether DistributivityRule's factoring should keep the derived filters for nested ORs below an AND root; currently the rule only fires on a root OR.
